title: Un-pin / condense the sticky toolbar on mobile
description:
styles.css:56 sets .view-toolbar { position: sticky; top: 0 }. Measured 547px tall at 412px wide = 60% of a 915px viewport and ~70% of a real Pixel 10's ~780px visible area. Confirmed pinning at top:0 across scrollY 400-1200, i.e. the entire range where any view is on screen. Usable height below it is 368px measured, ~233px on device - less than the 278px height of a single .view. The app's only content cannot fit on screen.

It stacks, vertically, at 412px: legend (3 items), 5 layer chips wrapping to 3 ragged right-aligned rows (105px), 2 pill switches + Undo/Redo, month label+slider+readout, scale label+slider+number input, and a 3-bar 'Scale reference' card with a hint line.
design:
Options:
- Drop position:sticky below ~960px, or keep only a ~56px condensed bar (month scrubber + a 'Controls' button) pinned and move the rest into a bottom sheet / <details> drawer.
- The month slider is the core interaction and the one control worth permanent space. Scale, layers, labels, lock, undo/redo and the legend are set-once-then-forget.
- Move the legend and 'Scale reference' card below the views or into the drawer.
- Collapse the scale row: #scaleInput duplicates #scaleSlider, and each view already renders its own '1 ft = N px' badge (.view-scale).
acceptance_criteria: At 412x915, a complete .view is visible on screen at the same time as whatever toolbar remains pinned.
close_reason: view-toolbar drops position:sticky below 960px, verified in 412x915 iframe

title: Tap a plant to open a species detail sheet
description:
On mobile there is no way to see species details by touch. Provable from source; a resized desktop browser has hover and will falsely appear to work.

- Details are delivered ONLY through native SVG <title> tooltips (src/render/tooltip.js -> renderTopView / renderElevationView). Confirmed 192 <title> elements for 192 plant groups. <title> never fires on touch.
- styles.css reinforces this with '.view svg [data-name]:hover { cursor: pointer }'.
- Species table cross-highlighting is bound to mouseenter/mouseleave (src/app.js:734-735) - hover-only.
- Clone is bound to contextmenu (src/app.js:522), and a document click handler at :541 hides the menu. Android long-press over SVG should be verified on-device rather than assumed, but there is no discoverable tap affordance either way.

Net: tapping a plant on a phone does nothing. The species table at the bottom of a 7-screen page is the only route to details and is disconnected from the plant you tapped.
design:
Add a click/pointerup handler on [data-plant-id] that opens a bottom sheet rendering buildTooltipLines(plant, state), plus a 'Clone' action - this reuses the existing tooltip builder and replaces the contextmenu-only clone path with something that works on both input types. Mirror mouseenter/mouseleave on species rows with click-to-pin highlighting. Keep the <title> elements: they remain the desktop tooltip and the accessible name.

Blast radius (codegraph impact buildTooltipLines): tooltip.js, topView.js, elevationViews.js, renderViews.js, tests/topView.test.js, tests/elevationViews.test.js.
acceptance_criteria: Tapping a plant in any of the three views opens a detail sheet with the same content the desktop tooltip shows, and offers Clone. No regression to the existing <title> tooltips.
close_reason: tap [data-plant-id] opens a bottom detail sheet (buildTooltipLines content) with a Clone action; verified via headless iframe at 412x915, existing SVG <title> tooltips unaffected

title: touch-action:none while unlocked swallows page scroll over every view
description:
src/interaction/dragController.js:170 and :349 set svg.style.touchAction = locked ? 'auto' : 'none'. Verified: with positions unlocked, all three view SVGs compute touch-action:none.

Each view is 370x278 inside a 412px column, so any vertical swipe that STARTS on a drawing is swallowed and the page will not scroll. With three views stacked, most of the scrollable area is dead. This is the single most maddening mobile behavior in the app, and is half the reason the scrolling feels 'nested'.

Locked is the default (lockToggle checked, no localStorage on first visit), so a first-time visitor will not hit this - but it makes editing on a phone effectively impossible.
design:
Either:
- use touch-action: pan-y instead of none while unlocked, so vertical page scroll survives and drags read as horizontal/hold gestures; or
- require a long-press (or tap-to-select-then-drag) to begin a touch drag, keeping touch-action:auto until that gesture is recognized.

Blast radius (codegraph impact createPlantDragController): dragController.js, src/app.js init.
acceptance_criteria: With positions unlocked on a touch device, a vertical swipe starting on a drawing scrolls the page, and dragging a plant still works.
close_reason: touch-action: pan-y instead of none, preserves vertical page scroll while unlocked

title: Renderers and drag controllers consume viewTransform; Scale slider becomes zoom
description:
Switch src/render/topView.js, src/render/elevationViews.js, and src/interaction/dragController.js off the global pixelsPerInch and onto createViewTransform(view).

pixelsPerInch stops being a render input entirely. The Edit-mode Scale slider becomes ZOOM — panel display size only, no effect on plant coordinates or background alignment. SCALE_LIMITS in src/constants.js is repurposed as zoom limits. #scaleIndicator's '3 in / 1 ft / 10 ft' bars read from the selected view's pxPerFt.

Drag clamping switches from viewBoxToFeet(viewBox.width, pixelsPerInch) to originFt + extentFt.
acceptance_criteria: With the migrated backyard project, plants render at pixel-identical positions to before. Dragging the Scale slider zooms panels while plants stay glued to the background photo. tests/topView.test.js and tests/elevationViews.test.js updated to the new signature; npm test and npm run test:e2e pass.
notes: normalizeProjectConfig now returns config.views[] AND a derived compat projection (config.plan / config.elevations / config.pixelsPerInch) built by legacyProjection() in src/data/projectConfig.js. That shim exists only so the app kept booting between beads — delete legacyProjection and its spread in normalizeProjectConfig once nl-tz7.3 and nl-tz7.4 have moved app.js, renderViews.js and viewConfig.js onto views[].
close_reason: Renderers and drag controllers now build geometry from createViewTransform(view); pixelsPerInch is gone as a render input. Scale slider is zoom (CSS grid track scaling only). The legacyProjection compat shim from nl-tz7.2 is deleted. npm test green; e2e 10/10; browser check confirmed panel 409->1253px with an identical plant path.

title: Config-driven view panels (no more hardcoded topView/frontView/sideView)
description:
The three panel names are baked in at more sites than the SVG refs:
  - index.html: #topSvg / #frontSvg / #sideSvg, data-view-panel='topView|frontView|sideView'
  - src/app.js:63-77: svgRefs.elevationSvgs and labelRefs built from literals
  - styles.css:779-781 and 1089-1091: maximize rules ENUMERATE all three names
  - configureViews / renderViews: positional mapping

Add a <template> to index.html, cloned once per views[] entry inside configureViews (already idempotent pure attribute/style assignment). renderViews loops views[] dispatching on type to renderTopView / renderElevationView. Keep id='topSvg' on the first plan view so existing e2e selectors keep working.

Maximize rules collapse to a generic .views[data-maximized] .view-panel.is-maximized, with refreshMaximizedView toggling the class; the data-maximized attribute stays for the container-level rules at styles.css 771/775/1100.
acceptance_criteria: A project.json declaring four views renders four panels, each maximizable. Backyard's three views look unchanged. Live preview works without a page reload: mutating appState.project then re-calling configureViews + render() is sufficient. npm run test:e2e passes.
close_reason: Panels are cloned from a <template> once per views[] entry; configureViews reconciles by view id so unchanged panels keep their SVG. Maximize CSS collapsed to .view-panel.is-maximized in both the desktop and mobile blocks. renderViews loops panels dispatching on type. Verified a 4-view project renders 4 maximizable panels against a scratch PUBLIC_DIR server; npm test and e2e 10/10 green.

title: views[] schema, legacy migration, and serializeProjectConfig
description:
Replace project.json's {plan, elevations[]} with a views[] array whose geometry is authored in feet.

Each view: { id, type: 'plan'|'elevation', viewFrom?, label, sublabel, viewBox {width,height}, originFt {x,y}, extentFt {width,height}, background|null, backgroundFrom? }

originFt is the yard coordinate at the viewBox bottom-left. On an elevation it replaces both pixel offsets: leftOffsetPx 80 -> originFt.x = -80/pxPerFt; bottomOffsetPx 100 -> originFt.y = -100/pxPerFt.

normalizeProjectConfig accepts BOTH shapes; legacy migrates with pxPerFt = defaultPixelsPerInch * 12. Writes always emit views[]. ELEVATION_SLOTS=2 goes away.

New serializeProjectConfig(config) omits values equal to defaults — normalizeProjectConfig inflates labels, sublabels and offsets, so writing the normalized object straight back would bloat every project file.

normalizeAssetPath currently THROWS on a missing background; relax it to allow null so a newly added view is valid before its image exists. Add the matching consumer branch in configureViews in the same commit — it sets container.style.backgroundImage unconditionally and would request projects/<slug>/null.
acceptance_criteria: pxPerFt = viewBox.width/extentFt.width must match viewBox.height/extentFt.height within tolerance; non-uniform views are rejected with a clear message. Path-traversal guard on background still holds. tests/projectConfig.test.js covers legacy->views[] migration, new-shape round-trip through serialize+normalize, default omission, and the validation errors; the /exactly 2 elevations/ assertion is removed.
close_reason: views[] schema + legacy migration + serializeProjectConfig landed. normalizeProjectConfig reads both shapes and also emits a derived legacy projection (plan/elevations/pixelsPerInch) so the app keeps working until nl-tz7.3/nl-tz7.4 rewire consumers. npm test (14 files) and npm run test:e2e (10 tests) both green.

title: Extract viewTransform.js — shared feet<->pixel math
description:
src/interaction/dragController.js (buildPointerContext), src/render/topView.js, and src/render/elevationViews.js each re-derive feet<->pixels independently. Extract one module so the setup tool, the renderers, and the drag controllers cannot drift.

New src/render/viewTransform.js:
  createViewTransform(view) -> {
    pxPerFt, toPx(feet), toFeet(px),
    planToViewBox({x,y}), viewBoxToPlan({x,y}),
    axisToX(axisFeet), xToAxis(px),
    groundY, orientation
  }

It WRAPS resolveElevationOrientation / elevationAxisToViewBoxX from src/render/elevationOrientation.js rather than replacing them, so the mirror/offset table stays in one place and tests/elevationOrientation.test.js keeps passing.
acceptance_criteria: tests/viewTransform.test.js exists and covers plan + all four elevation directions, mirrored and unmirrored, with non-zero originFt. Includes the regression-parity case: today's backyard values (pixelsPerInch 2.25, viewBox 800x600, bottomOffsetPx 100, leftOffsetPx 80, viewFrom east) produce pixel coordinates identical to the current formulas. npm test passes.
notes: Parity is covered in both directions: axisToX/planToViewBox against the renderer formulas (topView.js, elevationAxisToViewBoxX), and xToAxis/viewBoxToPlan against the drag-controller formulas (buildPointerContext.positionFeet, pointerAxisFeet). Expected values are built from legacy literals, never from the new transform, so the tests are not round-trip tautologies. 12 tests.
close_reason: src/render/viewTransform.js + tests/viewTransform.test.js added; 10 tests pass, full npm test green. Additive only — no consumers rewired (that is nl-tz7.3).

title: Viewport Setup Mode
description:
Add a third toolbar mode (Setup) for defining a project's views before plants are placed: create/remove/reorder views, set each view's real-world extent and origin in feet, pick backgrounds, place the elevation ground line and near edge, and cut zoomed detail crops of the plan. Config saves back to projects/<slug>/project.json via the persistence server.

Root problem: today project.json authors PIXELS (viewBox, bottomOffsetPx, leftOffsetPx) with feet->px coming from a global defaultPixelsPerInch that the Edit-mode Scale slider mutates at runtime. A calibration tool must not author pixels, so the schema inverts to feet-authored extentFt/originFt and the Scale slider is demoted to zoom.

Full plan: ~/.claude/plans/help-me-plan-for-jiggly-dragonfly.md
design:
project.json {plan, elevations[]} collapses into views[] with type: plan|elevation. A crop is just a plan view with non-zero originFt, a smaller extentFt, and backgroundFrom pointing at the full plan view. New src/render/viewTransform.js is the keystone: one shared feet<->pixel module wrapping the existing elevationOrientation.js mirror table, consumed by both renderers, both drag controllers, and the new setup controller.

No new runtime dependency: the app has no bundler (jszip is a raw script-tag global), the whole pipeline emits SVG with data-plant-id attributes the e2e suite asserts on, and dragController.js already solves pointer capture / screen->viewBox->feet / rAF re-render. Canvas libs (Konva, Fabric, Paper) would fork the render model. interact.js is the fallback only if handle code balloons past ~300 lines.
notes:
STATUS 2026-08-20 (session 3). Beads 1-7 and 9-12 are done. Only nl-tz7.8 (two-point ruler, optional P3) remains open.

SESSION 3: repaired fixture drift. The user drove the app and saved, which rewrote projects/example-frontyard/project.json without the 'street-bed' detail view and replaced planting_layout.csv. Restored street-bed (9x6 ft at (3,3), viewBox 180x120, backgroundFrom:'plan', label 'Street bed'); did NOT re-add rockrose-bed — the crop spec now derives the plants inside the rectangle from the CSV instead of naming one, and readLayoutRows() returns xFt/yFt for that. npm test and all 30 e2e specs pass. See nl-2p3 for the underlying fixture/live-project conflict.

The OPEN QUESTION about holly-corner sitting outside the shared yard bounds is moot: holly-corner is no longer in example-frontyard's layout, and the west elevation is now authored as viewFrom 'east' covering 25 ft. Re-raise only if new plants land outside resolveYardBounds().

ADDED SESSION 2
• src/render/backgroundCrop.js — resolveViewBackground(views, view) -> {path, crop}; the crop is fractions of the source image measured from its TOP-LEFT, derived by mapping the detail's corners through the SOURCE view's transform (handles mirrored elevations and the plan y-flip for free). cropToCssBackground() turns it into background-size/-position; captureViewToPng takes the same rect as sourceRect so screen and PNG agree.
• src/render/yardBounds.js — resolveYardBounds(views): first plan view's rectangle narrowed by the first elevation per compass direction. Both drag controllers take an optional getBounds. See nl-tz7.12's design field.
• projects/backyard converted to views[] (normalizes identically to the legacy file); projects/example-frontyard gained a fourth view, street-bed, a detail crop of the plan.

title: 'Maximize' is a no-op below 960px
description:
Clicking [data-maximize-target="topView"] at 412px leaves the view at exactly 370x278 - unchanged, measured before and after.

Cause: the max-width:960px breakpoint already sets .views { grid-template-columns: 1fr } (styles.css:905), so hiding the other two panels frees no width, and .view { aspect-ratio: var(--view-aspect-ratio, 4/3) } locks height to width. A tall phone cannot trade its width for height.

Three 'Maximize' buttons therefore occupy header space on mobile and deliver nothing.
design:
Options:
- On mobile make maximize mean full-viewport: position:fixed; inset:0 with aspect-ratio:auto, letting the SVG letterbox. The SVG already carries preserveAspectRatio='xMidYMid meet' (src/render/viewConfig.js), so this is mostly CSS.
- Or replace the three stacked panels with a swipeable/tabbed single view (Plan | South | East) so one drawing gets the whole column instead of a third of a 7-screen page.
- Add pinch-to-zoom / pan inside a maximized view: at 370px wide a 30ft yard renders plants a few pixels across and the species initials are unreadable.
acceptance_criteria: On a phone, maximizing a view makes it meaningfully larger than 370x278.
close_reason: maximized view goes position:fixed inset:0 with aspect-ratio:auto below 960px, verified view expands to fill viewport

title: Mobile UX overhaul (Pixel 10 class, ~412px viewport)
description:
The app is close to unusable on a phone. Measured in a 412x915 viewport against 'node server.js':

- Sticky .view-toolbar is 547px tall = 60% of a 915px viewport, ~70% of a real Pixel 10's ~780px visible area. It pins at top:0 for the whole scroll range where any drawing is on screen, leaving ~233px on device vs a 278px .view height. You cannot see one complete drawing while it is pinned.
- No tap path to species details exists at all (SVG <title> is hover-only).
- touch-action:none while unlocked swallows vertical scroll over every drawing.
- 'Maximize' is a no-op below 960px.
- Only one media query exists (max-width:960px); nothing targets phone width.
- Document is 6450px ~= 7 screens; 4615px of that is the species table.

No nested scroll containers and no horizontal overflow were found at 412px - the 'nested scroll' feeling comes from the pinned toolbar plus touch-action:none, not from a scroll container.

Full review with measurements: see child issues; each carries its own numbers.
design: Findings 2 and 3 (touch input) were argued from source, not browser automation: automated clicks are pointerType 'mouse' and a resized desktop window still has hover, so a browser check would have falsely shown them as working. Findings 1, 4, 5, 6 are browser-measured.
close_reason: All 7 mobile UX findings addressed: toolbar un-pinned, tap-to-detail sheet, touch scroll fixed, Maximize works below 960px, phone breakpoint added with clean chip wrapping, header trimmed + species cards collapsible, and tap-target/resize/scale-input polish. Verified via iframe testing at 412px and 1400px.

title: Project-scoped persistence endpoints
description: Scope /api/layout, /api/history, and /api/history/cursor to a project, resolving projects/<slug>/planting_layout.csv and layout-history.json. Validate the slug shape and confirm resolved paths stay inside the projects directory, since a client-supplied id now feeds a file path.
acceptance_criteria: Endpoints read/write the correct project files; traversal attempts and malformed slugs are rejected with 400; omitting the project falls back to the default.
close_reason: Closed

title: Make viewBox, offsets, and backgrounds per-project
description: Thread per-project viewBox dimensions and elevation offsets through configureViews, topView, elevationViews, and the bundle export instead of reading module-level constants. Move the hard-coded background URLs out of styles.css and app.js VIEW_BACKGROUNDS so they come from project config.
acceptance_criteria: No renderer reads PLAN_VIEWBOX/ELEVATION_VIEWBOX directly for geometry; constants remain only as defaults; backgrounds are applied from project config.
close_reason: Closed

title: Compass-direction elevation views
description: Generalize renderSouthElevation/renderEastElevation into one renderer driven by the compass direction the viewer stands on (north/south/east/west), deriving the horizontal yard axis, whether it is mirrored, and the front-to-back depth ordering. View labels come from project config instead of hard-coded index.html text, and the elevation drag controllers use the project-derived axis.
acceptance_criteria: Viewing from south/east reproduces today's output exactly; viewing from north/west mirrors the horizontal axis and reverses depth ordering; labels reflect config.
close_reason: Closed

title: Project config schema, loader, and on-disk migration
description: Add projects/index.json + projects/<slug>/project.json, a src/data/projectConfig.js loader that normalizes and validates config, and migrate the existing yard into projects/backyard/ (planting_layout.csv + img/).
acceptance_criteria: projectConfig parses and normalizes a config with defaults; invalid slugs and missing fields are rejected; existing backyard renders unchanged from its new location.
close_reason: Closed

title: Support multiple projects
description: Allow the app to host several landscape projects, each with its own background images, canvas dimensions, and compass orientation for the elevation views. plants.csv stays a shared global species catalog; each project has its own planting_layout.csv so its species selection is implicitly separate. Projects are authored on disk (projects/<slug>/) and chosen in-app via a picker that navigates to ?project=<slug>.
design: On-disk convention: projects/index.json lists projects; projects/<slug>/project.json declares viewBoxes, background images, default scale, and the compass direction each elevation is viewed from; projects/<slug>/planting_layout.csv holds placements; projects/<slug>/img/ holds backgrounds. Switching projects reloads the page with ?project=<slug> rather than re-initializing app state in place. Yard axes: origin SW, x increases east, y increases north.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add and remove plants in a layout
description: Edit mode can only move or clone existing plants. Add a way to place a new plant from the shared species catalog (plants.csv) and a way to delete a plant from the layout, both routed through the existing history/persistence commit path.
close_reason: Add plant picker in Edit mode; Remove on the detail sheet and right-click menu. Unit + e2e green.

title: Decide whether the yard has an extent separate from what a view covers
description:
Since nl-tz7.3, drag clamping uses each view's own originFt + extentFt. That fixed an upper-bound bug (the east elevation used to allow y=29.63, which rendered at 880px on an 800px viewBox) but introduced a lower bound below zero: the east elevation's originFt.x is -2.96, so a plant can be dragged to y=-2. The plan view starts at originFt {0,0}, so that plant renders at cy=654 on a 600px viewBox and disappears from the plan.

Views legitimately extend past the yard — an elevation's near-edge inset is margin, not plantable ground. So a view's extent is the wrong thing to clamp plant positions to. Either clamp every view to a shared yard extent, or accept per-view clamping and make the plan view show out-of-bounds plants somehow.

This is the same question nl-tz7.6 / nl-tz7.7 must answer when the setup UI lets someone move a view's origin under existing plants.
design: RESOLVED: clamp every view to a shared yard extent, not to the view's own rectangle. src/render/yardBounds.js resolveYardBounds(views) = the first plan view's rectangle, intersected with the axis range of the first elevation for each compass direction; later views of either kind are detail callouts and do not constrain (a plant outside a zoomed detail is not lost). An empty intersection falls back to the plan view rather than an inverted clamp range. Both drag controllers take an optional getBounds and fall back to the per-view extent when it is absent, so they still work standalone. Rejected alternative: keep per-view clamping and mark out-of-bounds plants in the plan — it leaves the plan lying about where a plant is. Checked both repo layouts against the new bounds: projects/backyard is entirely inside (bounds come out identical to the plan extent, and the old y=-2 hole in the east elevation is closed). projects/example-frontyard has one row, holly-corner at y=25.278, that sits 0.278 ft past the west elevation's 25 ft reach, so it snaps in by ~3 inches the first time it is dragged. That is the rule working: the plant is currently invisible in the west elevation. Left the data alone.
acceptance_criteria: A plant cannot be dragged into a position where it vanishes from another view. Whichever way it is resolved, the rule is stated in AGENTS.md alongside the axis/mirror table.
notes: OPEN QUESTION FOR THE USER (not a code bug): projects/example-frontyard's west elevation covers y 0..25 while its plan covers y 2..27, so the two disagree about the yard's north edge by 2 ft. holly-corner sits at y=25.278, outside the shared bounds, and will snap in by ~3.3 in the first time it is dragged (an ordinary undoable 'Moved plant' history entry). Left the data alone deliberately: widening the west view's extent or shifting its origin would slide its background photo out of alignment, and only the person who authored that photo knows which is right. Fix either by re-authoring the west view to cover y 2..27 or by nudging holly-corner to y<=25.
close_reason: Shared yard bounds implemented in src/render/yardBounds.js and consumed by both drag controllers via a new getBounds option; rule documented in AGENTS.md under Elevation orientation > Yard bounds; tests/yardBounds.test.js covers the near-edge margin, the narrowing elevation, detail views, the non-overlapping fallback, and a plan view with a non-zero origin.

title: Convert repo project.json files to views[] and update AGENTS.md
description:
Rewrite projects/backyard/project.json and projects/example-frontyard/project.json into the views[] shape (the legacy reader stays in place for anyone else's project files).

Update the Projects section of AGENTS.md: the viewFrom axis/mirror/depth table and the 'how to add a project' instructions both change, and originFt/extentFt replace bottomOffsetPx/leftOffsetPx/defaultPixelsPerInch. Note the new Setup mode as the preferred way to author a view. Mirror substantive edits into CLAUDE.md per the repo's own note that the two files are independent.
acceptance_criteria: Both projects load and render pixel-identically to before the conversion. AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md describe the views[] schema and Setup mode. Stashing one file back to the legacy shape still loads, proving the migration path.
notes: Do this LAST — it rewrites the project files every other spec is tested against. Note the user has ALREADY converted projects/example-frontyard by hand through the Setup UI (uncommitted at handoff time); check git status before redoing it. projects/backyard is still in the legacy {plan, elevations[]} shape and is what tests-e2e/app.spec.js and the scratch fixture rely on, so converting it means re-checking those. AGENTS.md's Projects section still documents defaultPixelsPerInch and the two-elevation rule; both are gone. Also add a fourth view to a repo project here so the multi-panel path gets permanent e2e coverage — nl-tz7.4 could only verify it against a throwaway server.
close_reason: projects/backyard/project.json converted to views[] — verified byte-for-byte equivalent by normalizing the old and new files and comparing (IDENTICAL), and locked in by a new test asserting 27 px/ft and the 80/100 px insets still fall where the legacy file put them. projects/example-frontyard was already converted by the user; added a fourth view to it, 'street-bed', a 9x6 ft detail at (3,3) with backgroundFrom:'plan', so the multi-panel and crop paths have permanent e2e coverage (new spec in tests-e2e/app.spec.js checks the panel count, the borrowed image, the crop percentages, that the uncropped plan keeps the stylesheet stretch, and that a plant inside the rectangle renders). AGENTS.md Projects section rewritten: views[] schema table, derived px/ft, Setup mode as the preferred authoring path, detail callouts, the legacy migration note, near-edge/mirroring wording, Scale-is-zoom, plus refreshed module list and e2e scratch-server guidance. CLAUDE.md multi-project paragraph mirrored.

title: backgroundFrom — crop a shared photo to a detail view's rectangle
description:
A crop view sets backgroundFrom: '<viewId>' instead of its own background, reusing the full plan photo cropped to its rectangle. Implemented in src/render/viewConfig.js as background-size / background-position arithmetic.

This is NOT the naive origin/fullExtent*100. CSS background-position: X% aligns the IMAGE's X% point with the CONTAINER's X% point, so the denominator is the leftover travel:

  sizeX% = full.extentFt.width  / crop.extentFt.width  * 100
  sizeY% = full.extentFt.height / crop.extentFt.height * 100
  posX%  = (crop.originFt.x - full.originFt.x) / (full.extentFt.width  - crop.extentFt.width)  * 100
  posY%  = 100 - (crop.originFt.y - full.originFt.y) / (full.extentFt.height - crop.extentFt.height) * 100

posY is inverted because plan y grows north while CSS y grows down. Both denominators are zero when the crop equals the full extent — guard and fall back to 0%. A crop must set background-size explicitly per panel; it cannot inherit the 100% 100% stretch at styles.css:876.
acceptance_criteria: A crop view with originFt {4,9} / extentFt {8,6} / backgroundFrom 'plan' shows exactly that patch of the plan photo, with the plants drawn over it landing on the same features they do in the full plan view. Unit test on the percentage math including the equal-extent guard.
notes:
Start here. The arithmetic is already worked out in the plan doc (~/.claude/plans/help-me-plan-for-jiggly-dragonfly.md) and is NOT the naive origin/fullExtent*100 — CSS background-position aligns the image's X% point with the container's X% point, so the denominator is the leftover travel:
  sizeX% = full.extentFt.width / crop.extentFt.width * 100
  posX%  = (crop.originFt.x - full.originFt.x) / (full.extentFt.width - crop.extentFt.width) * 100
  posY%  = 100 - (same with y)   // plan y grows north, CSS y grows down
Both denominators are zero when the crop equals the full extent — guard and fall back to 0%. styles.css sets background-size: 100% 100% on .view, so a crop must set background-size explicitly per panel rather than inherit the stretch.

Consumer is configureViews in src/render/viewConfig.js, which already resolves backgroundFrom's target by id (validation for an unknown id landed in nl-tz7.2). setupPanel.js already exposes a 'Borrow background from' select.
close_reason: New src/render/backgroundCrop.js resolves a view's background image and, for a backgroundFrom detail view, the patch of it to show. Consumed twice: viewConfig.js sets background-size/-position on the panel (and clears both when a view stops borrowing, since panels are reused by id), and app.js passes the same rect to captureViewToPng as a sourceRect so the exported PNG shows the same patch instead of the whole photo stretched. The crop is derived by mapping the detail's corners through the SOURCE view's transform, which handles mirrored elevations and the plan y-flip for free. normalizeProjectConfig now rejects backgroundFrom across differing type/viewFrom, and the Setup panel only offers compatible sources. tests/backgroundCrop.test.js covers the worked example, the equal-extent and full-width guards, and both mirrored and unmirrored elevations. Export loop over views[] was already in place from nl-tz7.4; crop backgrounds were the missing piece.

title: Setup mode shell — third toolbar mode and view list CRUD
description:
applyMode currently computes locked = mode !== 'edit' and persists a boolean under native-landscaping-positions-locked. Replace with a mode string under a new key native-landscaping-mode, migrating the old boolean on first read (true->view, false->edit).

Add a third [data-mode='setup'] button and a #setupRow sibling of #editRow. Plant drag controllers stay locked whenever mode !== 'edit', so the setup controller owns the pointer in Setup mode.

#setupRow contains: a view list with add / remove / reorder / duplicate, and a form for the selected view over label, sublabel, type, viewFrom, viewBox, extentFt, originFt, background / backgroundFrom. The numeric fields and the canvas are two views of the same state.
acceptance_criteria: Mode persists across reloads and old localStorage values migrate. Adding a view appends a panel live with no reload; removing one removes its panel. Edits in the form update the canvas immediately. Save round-trips through POST /api/project. A Playwright spec covers the mode switch; any spec that SAVES must point PUBLIC_DIR at a scratch copy — the suite is read-only by design and would otherwise rewrite projects/backyard/project.json.
notes: configureViews (src/render/viewConfig.js) reconciles panels by view id rather than rebuilding: a panel whose id is unchanged keeps its SVG element, so drag controllers stay bound and a live edit needs only 'mutate appState.project; configureViews(); render()'. That path is implemented but NOT yet exercised — nl-tz7.4 could not unit-test it (tests/helpers/fakeDom.js is an SVG-only stub and no jsdom is installed). Setup mode is its first real consumer: verify there that adding, removing, and reordering views does not orphan a drag controller.
close_reason: Setup mode shell landed: mode string under native-landscaping-mode with legacy boolean migration, third [data-mode=setup] button, #setupRow driven by src/interaction/setupPanel.js (view list with add/remove/reorder/duplicate plus a form over the selected view). Edits are validated through normalizeProjectConfig before being applied, so a rejected edit leaves the drawing on the last good state. Drag controllers gained destroy() and are rebuilt with the panels. 4 permanent e2e specs; save round-trip and drag-after-rebuild verified against a scratch PUBLIC_DIR.

title: Setup overlay and handle controllers — grid, crop rect, ground line, near edge
description:
New src/render/setupOverlay.js (guides drawn into the selected view's SVG) and src/interaction/setupController.js (handle dragging), both on top of viewTransform.js.

  - foot grid plus a dimension readout
  - plan/crop views: a draggable rect with 8 handles -> originFt / extentFt
  - elevation views: a draggable ground line -> originFt.y, and a draggable near-edge line -> originFt.x

Reuse the patterns dragController.js already establishes: pointer capture, rAF-throttled re-render, setLocked, a generous hit radius (MIN_HITBOX_RADIUS_PX = 28). Rect-handle and line-handle controllers should land around 100-150 lines each. If that balloons past ~300, interact.js is the sanctioned fallback — it is small, SVG-capable, and sits beside dragController.js rather than replacing it. Do NOT reach for a canvas library.
acceptance_criteria: Dragging the east elevation's ground line moves it live and plants' feet track it, no reload. Dragging a crop rect's handles updates originFt/extentFt and the numeric form in step. Overlay guides never appear outside Setup mode. tests/setupOverlay.test.js covers the guide geometry using tests/helpers/fakeDom.js.
notes: originFt.x is the axis value at the view's NEAR edge, not the left edge. For mirrored directions (north, west) axisToX maps originFt.x to viewBox.width — the right-hand side. The draggable near-edge line must read/write against the mirrored edge for those two directions, or it will be built backwards. The plan doc's inline comment ("axis value at left edge") is only true for south/east. See createViewTransform in src/render/viewTransform.js and its inversion test.
close_reason: setupOverlay.js (foot grid, dimension readout, plan extent rect with 8 handles, elevation ground and near-edge lines) and setupController.js (pointer capture, rAF coalescing with a flush on pointerup, 28px hit radius) both built on viewTransform. Overlay draws only in Setup mode and only on the selected view. 12 unit tests via fakeDom plus 3 e2e. No new dependency; controller is 154 lines, well under the interact.js threshold.

title: POST /api/project — persist view config to project.json
description:
Add config persistence alongside the existing layout persistence.

  - src/data/projectPaths.js: add configFile next to layoutFile / historyFile
  - server.js: POST /api/project?project=<slug>. Re-validate the body through normalizeProjectConfig server-side (server already imports from src/data/), FORCE id from the directory name — never trust the client — and write atomically (tmp file + rename)
  - src/data/persistence.js: client-side persistProjectConfig, injectable-fetch like its neighbours

No history/undo stack for config; the layout history machinery stays layout-only.
acceptance_criteria: Saving from the browser rewrites projects/<slug>/project.json in views[] form with no default-valued keys, and a reload reproduces the state. Invalid bodies are rejected with 400 and a readable message. A client-supplied id is ignored. tests/projectPaths.test.js covers configFile; persistence tests cover persistProjectConfig.
close_reason: configFile added to resolveProjectPaths; POST /api/project re-validates through normalizeProjectConfig with the id forced from the directory, writes atomically via tmp+rename, and serializes with serializeProjectConfig. Client persistProjectConfig added. Verified against a scratch PUBLIC_DIR: 200 writes views[] with no default keys and is a serialize/normalize fixed point, a hostile body id is ignored, a non-uniform view is a 400 with a readable message, no tmp files left, repo projects/ untouched. No UI triggers it yet — that is nl-tz7.6.

title: Add a real phone breakpoint and fix the ragged layer chips
description: styles.css has exactly ONE media query: max-width:960px. Below it, .view-toolbar__actions and .view-toolbar__control-group both keep min-width:280px (styles.css:82 and :91). At ~388px of content width two 280px boxes cannot share a row, so they wrap and stack. Confirmed no overflow results, but it is why the 5 layer chips land in three ragged right-aligned rows (105px tall).
design:
- Add a max-width:600px (or 640px) breakpoint for genuine phone layout.
- Below it, drop the min-width:280px floors and switch justify-content:flex-end / align-items:flex-end to stretch or flex-start, so chips form a clean full-width wrap or a horizontal scroller instead of ragged right-alignment.
- The 5 layer chips are 5 mutually-exclusive states of ONE setting - that is a segmented control or a <select>, not 5 buttons. Their long labels ('Hide trees + sculptural', 'Hide through accents') are also what forces the wrapping.
close_reason: Added max-width:600px breakpoint; dropped the 280px min-width floors on toolbar actions/control-group; chips now flex into a clean 2-col grid instead of ragged right-aligned rows. Verified via iframe at 412px.

title: Trim the header and collapse species cards
description:
The document is 6450px at 412px wide, about 7 screens.

- .page-header is 170px of the first screen and includes a .data-note paragraph about serving CSVs with 'npx serve' - developer instructions occupying ~20% of a phone's first screen.
- .species-table is 4615px: 12 species x ~385px, because the <=960px card layout renders all 10 columns as labelled rows per species.
design:
- Hide .data-note on mobile, or move it into the error-banner path, which is the only time it is actionable.
- Shrink h1 from 1.6rem; consider folding the project picker into the same condensed bar as the month scrubber.
- Make species cards collapsible: label + common name + botanical name by default, with height/width/growth form/sun/water/soil/bloom behind a <details> disclosure. That takes the block from ~4615px to roughly 900px.
- Once the tap-a-plant sheet exists, the species table becomes a browse surface rather than the only detail surface, and can be a compact list.
close_reason: Hid dev-only .data-note and shrank h1 to 1.15rem on phone (<=600px). Species cards now default to label+botanical+common name with a per-row 'Details' toggle revealing height/width/growth-form/sun/water/soil/bloom; table height for 12 species dropped from ~4615px to ~2061px collapsed. Desktop table (>960px) unchanged - verified 10 columns, toggle cell display:none, in a 1400px iframe.

title: Add Playwright end-to-end browser tests
description: No automated browser tests exist; tests/ is all node --test unit tests with a fake DOM. Add Playwright e2e specs that boot server.js and assert on rendered SVG DOM (not screenshots) so agents need not drive Chrome manually.
close_reason: Closed

title: Remove four-nerve daisies from backyard layout
description: Two four-nerve-daisy-front rows in projects/backyard/planting_layout.csv should be deleted.
close_reason: Closed

title: Tests and docs for multi-project support
description: Cover project config parsing, compass-direction elevation geometry, and server project path resolution. Update tests/persistence.test.cjs for the project-scoped URL, and update AGENTS.md (mirrored into CLAUDE.md) for the new on-disk layout.
acceptance_criteria: npm test passes; AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md describe projects/ and how to add a project.
close_reason: Closed

title: Project picker UI and ?project= routing
description: Add a project selector to the header that navigates to ?project=<slug>; app.js resolves the active project from the query string, falling back to the default in projects/index.json.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a project reloads into that project; an unknown or missing slug falls back to the default with a visible notice.
close_reason: Closed

title: example-frontyard is both a shipped test fixture and the user's live project
description: Repo tests pin geometry and plant ids in projects/example-frontyard, but the same project is editable in the running app: Setup-mode Save rewrites project.json and a drag rewrites planting_layout.csv. On 2026-08-20 a Save dropped the 'street-bed' detail view, breaking tests/projectConfig.test.js and the crop e2e spec; the layout CSV was curated at the same time, removing rockrose-bed. Move the multi-panel/crop coverage onto the scratch fixture (tests-e2e/scratch-fixture.mjs already builds a throwaway root) or onto a project that is not user-editable, so ordinary use of the app cannot fail the suite.
acceptance_criteria: No test in tests/ or tests-e2e/ asserts on geometry or plant ids that live in a project the user edits through the UI. Editing example-frontyard in the app and saving leaves npm test and npm run test:e2e green.

title: Verify the long-press clone/remove menu on a real touch device
description: The context menu opens on the native contextmenu event, which on touch means long-press. CDP's Input.dispatchTouchEvent does not synthesize contextmenu, so tests-e2e/touch.spec.js cannot cover it either way — a hold delivers only pointerdown/pointerup/click. Two things worth checking on an actual phone: whether long-press still reaches the menu now that the SVG is touch-action:none in Edit mode, and whether handlePointerDown's event.preventDefault() suppresses it when the press lands on a plant. Not a known break; unverified. The touch route to Clone/Remove is covered: a tap in View mode opens the detail sheet, which carries both.

title: Drag and setup controllers both write svg.style.cursor
description: Same shared-element bug as the touch-action one just fixed (both controllers own the same SVG and the last writer wins), but for cursor. applyMode unlocks the drag controller (cursor: grab), then syncSetupOverlay re-locks the setup controller, which resets it to default. So Edit mode never shows the grab cursor on desktop. Cosmetic only; touch-action was fixed by giving each controller its own class, and cursor wants the same treatment.

title: Emptying a layout discards its history on reload
description: persistLayout now accepts an empty plants array, so removing the last plant does reach disk. But loadLayoutHistory -> findHistoryEntryIndexByLayout returns -1 for an empty layout CSV (it bails on a blank string), so the next page load reports 'History diverged from planting_layout.csv' and throws the history stack away. Degrades quietly; only reachable by removing every plant.

title: Setup mode authors feet; viewBox is derived
description:
Resolved the open question in the plan doc's Design section 8 ('derive viewBox from extentFt — decide when building bead 6').

The first cut of the setup form locked extentFt to the viewBox's aspect ratio, so typing a height silently rewrote the width — you could never say '30 ft by 10 ft'. Wrong value derived.

Now extentFt is authored freely in both directions and viewBox = extentFt * a per-view resolution (px per ft). Aspect ratio is whatever the extent says, and the non-uniform view createViewTransform rejects is unreachable from the form rather than merely guarded against. The two pixel fields collapsed into one 'Resolution (px per ft)' knob, with the derived drawing size shown as a hint.

normalizeProjectConfig and serializeProjectConfig still read and write an authored viewBox, so hand-edited project.json files are unaffected.
acceptance_criteria: Setting Width (ft) then Height (ft) leaves both at what was typed; covered in tests-e2e/app.spec.js.
close_reason: Landed with the drag-coverage commit.

title: Upload background images through the UI
description:
DEFERRED from nl-tz7. Setup mode expects background images to be dropped into projects/<slug>/img/ by hand, with the relative path typed into the form. A file-picker upload endpoint would remove that step.

Needs multipart handling in server.js (which is currently JSON-only), an allowlist of image types matching MIME_TYPES, a size cap, and the same path-traversal guard resolveProjectPaths already applies.

title: Yard feature drawing (beds, hardscape, house footprint)
description:
DEFERRED — deliberately out of scope for the Viewport Setup Mode epic (nl-tz7), and nothing in that epic blocks this.

Beds, borders, hardscape, house footprint, paths, and existing trees are yard geometry in FEET shared across every view — different in kind from per-view presentation config, so they do not belong in project.json. They get their own file, projects/<slug>/features.json, their own render module drawn beneath plants, and their own endpoint.

Rendering a feature into an elevation reuses viewTransform / resolveElevationOrientation, so the mirror/offset math stays in exactly one place. Depends on nl-tz7.1 landing viewTransform.js.
design: Separate file, separate render module, separate endpoint. Drawn beneath the plant layer in every view. The polygon-vertex editing controller can follow the same shape as the rect/line handle controllers from nl-tz7.7.

title: Export bundle loops over views[]
description:
captureViewToPng (src/export/viewCapture.js) is per-SVG and needs no change, but its caller at src/app.js:317 enumerates the three panels by hand ({ view: project.plan, svg: svgRefs.topSvg, fileName: 'plan-view.png' }, ...). Move that loop to views[].

Crop views ARE included in the export — a detail callout is exactly the kind of thing worth having as a PNG. File names come from the view id: plan-view.png, shade-bed-view.png, east-view.png.
acceptance_criteria: Exporting a project with four views yields four PNGs named from view ids, each with its background composited. Existing three-view export output is unchanged apart from any id-derived renaming.
notes: Partly done already: nl-tz7.4 replaced the hand-enumerated export panel list with a loop over the cloned viewPanels, so crop views are included automatically. That also renamed the files — elevations went from <id>-elevation.png to <id>-view.png, matching the plan doc's plan-view.png / shade-bed-view.png scheme. What remains here is whatever naming or per-view export options this bead still wants on top.
close_reason: New src/render/backgroundCrop.js resolves a view's background image and, for a backgroundFrom detail view, the patch of it to show. Consumed twice: viewConfig.js sets background-size/-position on the panel (and clears both when a view stops borrowing, since panels are reused by id), and app.js passes the same rect to captureViewToPng as a sourceRect so the exported PNG shows the same patch instead of the whole photo stretched. The crop is derived by mapping the detail's corners through the SOURCE view's transform, which handles mirrored elevations and the plan y-flip for free. normalizeProjectConfig now rejects backgroundFrom across differing type/viewFrom, and the Setup panel only offers compatible sources. tests/backgroundCrop.test.js covers the worked example, the equal-extent and full-width guards, and both mirrored and unmirrored elevations. Export loop over views[] was already in place from nl-tz7.4; crop backgrounds were the missing piece.

title: Two-point ruler calibration from the background photo (optional)
description:
OPTIONAL — the user asked to explore photo calibration without committing to it. Ship the rest of the epic first; this is a recommendation because it is unusually cheap, not a requirement. Dropping it leaves the numeric extentFt field doing the same job.

Three gestures cover the whole of 'calibrate against a photo', with no homography, no new data model, and no OpenSeadragon:
  - drag across a known length in the photo, type the real length -> solves pxPerFt, hence extentFt
  - click the ground line -> originFt.y   (covered by nl-tz7.7)
  - click the near edge   -> originFt.x   (covered by nl-tz7.7)

This bead is the ruler only. styles.css:876 is background-size: 100% 100%, so viewBox units map proportionally onto the image and the measurement is well-posed.
acceptance_criteria: Dragging the ruler across a fence panel of known length and entering that length updates extentFt, and the view re-scales so the plan matches the photo. Unit-tested math for the solve.

title: Mobile polish: tap targets, resize thrash, numeric scale input
description:
Smaller items from the mobile review.

- Tap targets below the 44px guideline: chips 31px tall, #projectSelect 29px, .view-panel__toggle ~24px. Pill switches at 46px are fine.
- window.addEventListener('resize', render) (src/app.js:520): Android's address bar showing/hiding and the keyboard opening on #scaleInput both fire resize, causing a full re-render of 192 plant groups x 3 views mid-scroll. Debounce it, or compare dimensions before re-rendering.
- #scaleInput is type='number' with step='0.01' - opens a numeric keypad and is fiddly on touch. On mobile the slider alone (plus the per-view '1 ft = N px' badge) is enough.

NOT a problem, checked and confirmed fine: the drag hitbox. MIN_HITBOX_RADIUS_PX = 28 (dragController.js:3) is multiplied by scaleFactor = viewBox / rect (:362, :418), so it is 28 SCREEN px regardless of render size. No small-screen inversion; a 56px-diameter target is acceptable.
close_reason: Tap targets (chips, view-panel__toggle, projectSelect) bumped to 44px min-height on phone (<=600px). Resize handler debounced 150ms and skips re-render when innerWidth is unchanged, so address-bar show/hide and keyboard-open no longer force a full 192-group x3-view re-render. #scaleInput (numeric keypad) hidden on phone; slider + per-view badge remain. Verified in-browser at 412px.

title: Layout history seeds bypass parsePlantLayoutCsv validation
description: appState.plants can come from layoutHistoryInstance.getCurrentPlants() (src/app.js), which is seeded from the server's layout-history.json. Those entries are plain plant arrays and never pass through parsePlantLayoutCsv, so the duplicate-id constraint added in nl-92d does not cover them. Not reachable today: cloning routes through buildCloneId, CSV load now throws, and a scan of projects/example-frontyard/layout-history.json (6 entries) found no duplicates. Worth closing if a future path writes history directly.
acceptance_criteria: Either history seeds are validated on load, or a note records why the path is safe by construction.
close_reason: Not worth pursuing; path is safe by construction (no known way to write history without going through validated CSV load/clone flow)

title: Duplicate plant id in backyard planting_layout.csv
description: projects/backyard/planting_layout.csv has two rows sharing the id 'four-nerve-daisy-front' (lines 26 and 27). Ids are used to look up plants for dragging, cloning, and hover/target highlighting, so the second row is effectively unreachable — dragging either silhouette moves the first match. Pre-existing, found while verifying the multi-project change; not caused by it.
acceptance_criteria: Every id in planting_layout.csv is unique; consider validating uniqueness in parsePlantLayoutCsv.
close_reason: Duplicates already removed by nl-y8y; parsePlantLayoutCsv now throws on repeated ids, with unit tests.
